description: dns.createRecord (POST /v2/domains/{domain}/records) models its body as a per-record-type anyOf whose arms the request-body flattener drops, leaving only the top-level `type` property — name/value/ttl/mxPriority/srv/https/comment never reach CreateRecordRequest. Replace the requestBody schema with the flat merged object (field template: the already-correct updateRecord shape). All fields optional except `type`; per-type value constraints (ipv4/ipv6 formats, MX requiring mxPriority, SRV/HTTPS requiring their sub-objects) are enforced server-side.

type.description: The type of record, it could be one of the valid DNS records.

name.description: A subdomain name or an empty string for the root domain. Required for every record type except SRV and HTTPS, whose name is derived from srv/https.

value.description: The record value (address, hostname, or text depending on the record type). Not used for SRV and HTTPS records, which use the srv/https objects instead.

ttl.description: The TTL value. Must be a number between 60 and 2147483647. Default value is 60.

mxPriority.description: The MX priority value of the DNS record. Required for MX records.

srv.description: The SRV record payload. Required for SRV records.

https.description: The HTTPS record payload. Required for HTTPS records.

comment.description: A comment to add context on what this DNS record is for
comment.example: used to verify ownership of domain
